levels.title: Resilience and operations
levels.description: Retries, circuit breakers and hot config reload with pico-resilience.

levels.title: Absorbing failures with @retryable
levels.description:
Retry as a decorator

Transient failures (a busy gateway, a flaky feed) should be invisible to callers. @retryable re-invokes the method until it succeeds or attempts run out, and only for the exception types you list in retry_on - everything else propagates immediately.

The feed below fails twice before every success. Add the decorator so the service call succeeds and the caller never notices.

files.name: app.py
main.py
files.content:
import pico_ioc as pico
from pico_ioc import DictSource, configuration
import app

CONFIG = {"resilience": {"enabled": True}}
container = pico.init(
    # A real app uses pico_boot.init(modules=[app]) and gets these two for
    # free. The lab lists them so it only ever loads what this lesson needs.
    modules=["pico_resilience", "pico_ioc.event_bus", app],
    config=configuration(DictSource(CONFIG)),
)

service = container.get(app.QuoteService)
result = service.quote()
feed = container.get(app.FlakyFeed)

print(f"quote: {result}")
print(f"attempts underneath: {feed.calls}")
assert result == {"spot": 101.25}
assert feed.calls == 3, "expected 2 absorbed failures + 1 success"
print("retry absorbed the hiccups")

hints: Import retryable from pico_resilience (already imported) and stack it on quote().
retry_on takes a tuple of exception types.
The feed only recovers on its third call, so the policy has to allow that many.

levels.title: Failing fast with @circuit_breaker
levels.description:
Stop hammering a dead dependency

Retry helps with hiccups; it makes outages worse. A circuit breaker counts consecutive failures and, past failure_threshold, rejects calls instantly with CircuitOpenError - the dependency gets air, your threads get their time back.

Run the lab: after three failing calls the breaker opens, and the fourth call never reaches the feed (its call counter stays frozen).

files.name: app.py
main.py
files.content:
import pico_ioc as pico
from pico_ioc import DictSource, configuration
from pico_resilience import CircuitOpenError
import app

container = pico.init(
    # A real app uses pico_boot.init(modules=[app]) and gets these two for
    # free. The lab lists them so it only ever loads what this lesson needs.
    modules=["pico_resilience", "pico_ioc.event_bus", app],
    config=configuration(DictSource({"resilience": {"enabled": True}})),
)

service = container.get(app.QuoteService)
feed = container.get(app.DeadFeed)

for attempt in range(3):
    try:
        service.quote()
    except app.FeedDown:
        print(f"attempt {attempt + 1}: feed down (breaker counting)")

calls_when_open = feed.calls
try:
    service.quote()
except CircuitOpenError as e:
    print(f"breaker open: {e}")

assert feed.calls == calls_when_open, "an open breaker must not call the feed"
print(f"feed calls frozen at {feed.calls}")

hints: CircuitOpenError is raised by the breaker itself; the feed is never invoked once open.

levels.title: Hot reload: policies change while running
levels.description:
refresh_config()

Resilience policies follow live configuration. Mutate the config source and call container.refresh_config(): it returns the set of changed prefixes and the interceptors pick the new values up immediately - no restart. With resilience.enabled = false the same flaky call now fails on the first attempt.

Complete the marked line to re-enable resilience at the end.

files.name: app.py
main.py
files.content:
import pico_ioc as pico
from pico_ioc import DictSource, configuration
import app

CONFIG = {"resilience": {"enabled": True}}
container = pico.init(
    # A real app uses pico_boot.init(modules=[app]) and gets these two for
    # free. The lab lists them so it only ever loads what this lesson needs.
    modules=["pico_resilience", "pico_ioc.event_bus", app],
    config=configuration(DictSource(CONFIG)),
)
service = container.get(app.QuoteService)
feed = container.get(app.FlakyFeed)

print("with retry:", service.quote(), f"({feed.calls} attempts)")

CONFIG["resilience"]["enabled"] = False
changed = container.refresh_config()
print(f"changed: {sorted(changed)}")
assert changed == frozenset({"resilience"})

before = feed.calls
try:
    service.quote()
except app.QuoteUnavailable:
    print(f"without retry: failed after {feed.calls - before} attempt")
assert feed.calls == before + 1

CONFIG["resilience"]["enabled"] = True
# TODO: flipping the dict is not enough - the interceptor still holds the
# old value. Make the call below survive the hiccups again.
print("with retry again:", service.quote())

levels.title: Operating it: actuator, probes and refresh over HTTP
levels.description:
From library to operations

In a deployed service the same mechanics are driven over HTTP by pico-actuator:

  • POST /actuator/refresh is the HTTP face of refresh_config(): change the config source, hit the endpoint, and the response lists the changed prefixes - the previous lab, operable from a terminal.
  • /actuator/health aggregates health indicators; wire one to business state (queue depth, broker connectivity) and your load balancer stops routing to a saturated instance before it fails.
  • /actuator/metrics serves the prometheus default registry, shared with pico-otel.

Runnable, tested versions of both patterns live in pico-examples: runtime-config (hot reload through the actuator, with the failure mode asserted) and observability-service (health driven by business state, metrics and traces).
